_readme: Single source of truth for the project-specific values baked into this template. 'values' holds the CURRENT values (template defaults until you initialize). Run scripts/Initialize-Template.ps1 (or the 'bc-init' Copilot agent) to replace them across the repo and rewrite this file with your choices. 'tokens' documents what each value means and where it appears.

extraTools._readme: Project-specific tool IDs merged into every agent and prompt 'tools:' list AFTER each template sync (scripts/Update-FromTemplate.ps1) and at init time, so your custom MCP servers survive the refresh that overwrites those files. 'all' applies to every agent + prompt; 'agents'/'prompts' add per-file extras keyed by file name without extension (e.g. 'bc-dev', 'onboard-app'). Additive only - tools are never removed. Prefer generic namespaces (e.g. 'al/*'); purely machine-local servers can instead just be toggled per-session in VS Code's tool picker.

models._readme: Model assigned to each agent's frontmatter 'model:' field. Each value MUST match a name in your Copilot model picker exactly (e.g. 'Claude Sonnet 4.6', 'Claude Opus 4.8', 'GPT-5.5'). Some environments need a ' (copilot)' suffix — add it if VS Code flags the model as unknown. Run scripts/Initialize-Template.ps1 or the 'bc-init' agent to write these into .github/agents/*.agent.md.

tokens.appPrefix: BC partner/app object-name prefix. Appears in AL object names ('ABC Payment ...'), identifiers, file names, app.json publisher-style prefix, instructions and docs.
tokens.ticketPrefix: Work-item key used in 'PREFIX-123' references and 'feature/PREFIX-{ID}-*' / 'bugfix/' / 'hotfix/' branch names. Often equal to appPrefix but can differ (e.g. ADO project key); set to '' for bare IDs. Note: spec folders no longer carry this prefix — they are organised by module/area as 'specs/<Area>/<type>-<ID>-<slug>/'.
tokens.appName: Display name of the sample AL extension (app.json 'name').
tokens.objectIdFrom: Lower bound of your assigned AL object ID range. The initializer shifts every sample object ID by (new from - old from).
tokens.objectIdTo: Upper bound of your assigned AL object ID range.
tokens.repoSlug: GitHub 'owner/repo' slug. Appears in app.json url, issue-template config, docs.
tokens.adoOrg: Azure DevOps organization name (used by .vscode/mcp.json and docs).
tokens.workItemSystem: 'ADO' or 'GitHub'. When 'GitHub', the initializer converts ADO 'AB#123' commit-linking syntax to GitHub '#123'.
tokens.branchingStrategy: Identifier for the branching model documented in docs/branching-strategy.md. Default 'feature-release-selective'.
tokens.environments: Ordered list of BC environment names referenced by the deploy workflow (default TEST -> PROD).
tokens.bcVersion: Target Business Central version for the sample AL app. 'application'/'platform' are app.json minimums (e.g. '28.0.0.0' for 2026 wave 1) and 'runtime' is the AL runtime (e.g. '16.0'). The initializer writes these into app/app.json and test/app.json. Symbols are pulled from the public MSSymbolsV2 feed (see docs/al-agent-tools.md). Bump these when you move to a newer BC release.
tokens.bcQuality: Optional Microsoft BCQuality knowledge base (https://github.com/microsoft/BCQuality) used to back AL review. 'enabled' on/off; 'mode' is 'vendor' (tracked copy in this repo) or 'submodule'; 'path' is the checkout folder. Run scripts/Add-BCQuality.ps1 to fetch it. See docs/bcquality.md.
tokens.sync: Controls how template updates are applied by scripts/Update-FromTemplate.ps1 and .github/workflows/template-sync.yml. 'customizationsPath' is the folder that holds the VS Code-discoverable Copilot customizations (.github/agents, .github/skills, .github/prompts, .github/instructions, .github/copilot-instructions.md and the agent meta-docs AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md / WHEN-TO-USE.md / SKILLS.md): '.' keeps them at the repo root (default); set it to a subfolder (e.g. 'app') to place them under <path>/.github so they are discovered when you open that folder directly; the specs/_TEMPLATE scaffold (to <path>/specs) and the .vscode editor configs (to <path>/.vscode, so launch/tasks/mcp/extensions apply when you open that folder) follow too. When not set explicitly, scripts/Install-IntoExistingRepo.ps1 auto-detects an existing subfolder layout (e.g. app/.github) and reuses it. 'syncWorkflow' true = install/refresh the GitHub Actions template-sync workflow (.github/workflows/template-sync.yml + .templatesyncignore); false = skip it (auto-defaulted for Azure DevOps-only repos, where a GitHub Action never runs) and rely on scripts/Update-FromTemplate.ps1 for ongoing sync. GitHub platform files (.github/workflows, ISSUE_TEMPLATE, PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE) always stay at the repo root so Actions and Copilot on github.com keep working. 'updateModels' false = keep your agent 'model:' choices (re-applied from this file after each sync); true = accept the template's model recommendations. 'updateExtensions' false = keep your .vscode/extensions.json toolset; true = pull the template's recommended list. 'updateInstructions' true = pull AL coding-standard instruction updates; false = keep your edited instructions. 'include' is a set of on/off switches for optional content categories, honored by BOTH the installer and every later sync so excluded content is never (re-)added: 'metaDocs' = the agent-architecture reference (.github/AGENT-ARCHITECTURE.md, WHEN-TO-USE.md, SKILLS.md); 'referenceDocs' = the docs/ reference library (bcquality, branching-strategy, workflow, al-agent-tools, spec-driven-development, al-go-upgrade); 'issueOps' = the GitHub-issue-driven pipeline (.github/workflows/issue-*.yml, ISSUE_TEMPLATE, ISSUE_ORCHESTRATION.md) - turn off when you drive work from ADO or elsewhere; 'specs' = the specs/_TEMPLATE scaffold; 'prTemplate' = .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md; 'sampleApp' = the demo app/ + test/ projects (install-time only; ongoing sync never touches your AL source). Core files (agents, skills, prompts, instructions, copilot-instructions.md, template.config.json, the sync scripts) are always included. The template ships these all-on; scripts/Install-IntoExistingRepo.ps1 writes a leaner profile into an existing repo (metaDocs/referenceDocs/issueOps/sampleApp off) which you can change during its     -Configure step. 'components' is a per-component policy shared by the BC ALM VS Code extension and every sync: 'disabled' = component ids that are never installed or updated (the extension moves their files to .bc-alm/disabled/), 'keepLocal' = component ids whose local version you own (never updated, still listed). Ids: agent:<name>, skill:<folder>, prompt:<name>, instruction:<name>, doc:<name>, workflow:<name>, file:<path> (e.g. 'agent:bc-deploy', 'skill:bc-ship-release'). Syncs also record the template commit and hashes of every installed file in template.lock.json (commit it): with that baseline, files you edited are kept and reported instead of overwritten, and the lock's first source (your fork or your own template) becomes the default sync source.
tokens.extraTools: Project-specific tool IDs re-applied to agent/prompt 'tools:' lists after every template sync so they are not lost when those files are overwritten. 'all' = added to every agent and prompt; 'agents'/'prompts' = per-file additions keyed by file name without extension. Captured by scripts/Initialize-Template.ps1 and merged by scripts/Update-FromTemplate.ps1. Additive only (never removes tools).

modelsToken: The 'models' object maps each agent file name (without .agent.md) to the model written into its 'model:' frontmatter line. Edit values here, then re-run the initializer to apply them across .github/agents/.
